summary: A 2 Å titanium sacrificial layer deposited on sputtered α-tantalum acts as an oxygen getter to chemically reduce the native Ta oxide at the metal-air interface; after removal by buffered oxide etchant and high-vacuum annealing at 700°C for 10 hours, tantalum coplanar waveguide resonators on high-resistivity silicon exhibit internal quality factors $Q_i$ exceeding 1.5 million at single-photon occupancy, representing a 2–4× improvement over otherwise identical devices without the titanium layer. The method directly addresses two-level system losses at the metal-air interface, achieving extracted TLS loss tangents $F	anlap{/}{ule{2pt}{0.4pt}}	ext{ }aisebox{-0.4ex}{δ}_{	ext{TLS}}$ as low as $0.58 	imes 10^{-6}$ and $Q_i$ values exceeding 2 million at low power and 13 million at high photon occupancy on optimized samples.
motivation: Two-level system losses at the metal-air interface of tantalum-based superconducting circuits remain a limiting factor for qubit coherence despite tantalum's superior native oxide compared to niobium; conventional capping layers leave additional interfaces that can introduce losses rather than suppress them.
method: An ultrathin titanium film (2 Å) is deposited in situ on α-tantalum under high vacuum, serving as a kinetic barrier and oxygen scavenger during subsequent CF₄-based reactive ion etching and lithography steps; the titanium layer is then selectively removed via buffered oxide etch (20 min) followed by 700°C annealing for 10 hours in high vacuum, leaving a chemically modified, reduced tantalum oxide surface.
